paragraphs: The Microlino opens at the front, like the bubble cars of the fifties it is openly copying, and that single door is not nostalgia for its own sake: it lets the car park nose in to a kerb and let people out onto the pavement. Everything about the design assumes a city and nothing else.
The model holds 184,104 polygons and 190,441 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, finished in white, and carries StemCell certification.
At $129 it suits urban mobility visualisation, automotive marketing, architectural and street scenes, advertising, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A sunroof is one of the few options that changes the roofline itself, and in a render it changes the reflection across the whole upper body. Blue makes that obvious: a colour that shows every crease in the panelwork and every highlight the glass throws back.
The model holds 257,665 polygons and 278,292 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification. Rigged and simplified builds are offered separately.
At $129 it suits architectural and street visualisation, automotive marketing, configurators, advertising, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Duke 390 is a small capacity bike built with the geometry of a much angrier one. Short wheelbase, high bars, no fairing to hide behind: it made a category of riders who wanted the handling of a supermoto without the licence or the insurance bill.

The model holds 120,601 polygons and 124,749 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps, 9 of them at 8192x8192 and 4 at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits motorcycle marketing and configurators, street and architectural scenes, advertising, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

Sprint cars without wings are the purer and more frightening version of the discipline. The wing is what glues a sprint car to a dirt oval; take it off and the driver has only the throttle and the steering to hold the thing sideways through a corner.
The model is supplied in red and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification. Green and blue builds are offered separately for grids and field scenes.
At $129 it suits motorsport visualisation and broadcast graphics, advertising, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

A steam locomotive is a boiler that happens to have wheels, and everything visible on it, the rods, the domes, the sandboxes, is plumbing made external because there was nowhere else to put it. Coupled to a freight wagon, it becomes the whole nineteenth century economy in two objects.
The model holds 835,781 polygons and 649,770 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the locomotive together with the wagon. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits railway history and museum work, period film and television, documentary and education material, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A load properly strapped down says more about a scene than the vehicle does. Ratchet straps over a pallet, corners protected, weight over the axle: it turns a pickup from a lifestyle prop into a working vehicle in the middle of a job.
The model holds 506,077 polygons and 541,608 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the truck together with its secured load. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits logistics and trade visualisation, construction and delivery scenes, safety and training material, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Recycling plastic is mostly a sorting problem, not a chemistry one. The plant is a sequence of machines for separating one polymer from another by density, colour and shape, and the shredders and extruders at the end are almost an afterthought by comparison.
The scene holds 279,072 polygons and 305,654 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.

At $129 it suits environmental and waste management visualisation, industrial and infrastructure presentation, education and documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Rural and highway policing runs on pickups rather than saloons, because the job involves unpaved roads and carrying equipment. A generic scheme keeps it usable anywhere: no force insignia to place the vehicle in a jurisdiction it does not belong to.

The model holds 282,757 polygons and 322,476 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with a simple interior, textured with 9 maps, 8 at 4096x4096 and one at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $129 it suits law enforcement and public safety visualisation, street and architectural scenes, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

A cell with a skeleton in it needs no caption. It is an image with one meaning, used in horror, in historical work about forgotten prisoners, and in games that want the player to understand what happened here without a line of dialogue.

This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the prison space together with the skeleton as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification, and a second volume of the set is offered separately.
At $129 it suits horror and thriller production, game environments, historical and documentary work, museum material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The Wilga looks wrong until you know what it is for. Enormously long undercarriage legs, a wing that generates lift at walking pace, and a fuselage shaped for glider towing and parachute drops from a grass strip. Every awkward proportion on it has a job.
The airframe holds 240,195 polygons and 249,621 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in white, and carries StemCell certification. A yellow scheme is offered separately.
At $129 it suits general aviation visualisation, flight simulation, aviation history and documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

The Ripsaw is a tracked vehicle built to the logic of a race car: suspension travel measured in feet, a power to weight ratio no armoured vehicle would tolerate, and a crew position placed for speed rather than protection. It exists somewhere between a prototype and a toy for people with serious money.
The model holds 660,857 polygons and 699,569 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification. A simplified build is offered separately for background use.
At $129 it suits defence and technology visualisation, advertising, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

An airport fire vehicle has one requirement above all others: be anywhere on the field within three minutes. That is why the Panther accelerates like nothing else of its weight, carries its own water and foam, and puts a roof monitor where a ladder would be on a municipal appliance.
The model is built at subdivision level, 335,820 polygons and 370,646 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification. A rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits airport and emergency services visualisation, safety and training material, aviation scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2020.

The Superjet was Russia's first commercial airliner designed after the Soviet era, built with international suppliers and then forced to replace most of them. The long range variant is the version that made the aircraft usable on routes it was originally too limited for.
The airframe holds 172,491 polygons and 188,390 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in flight configuration. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $129 it suits aviation visualisation, flight simulation, news and documentary graphics, film backgrounds and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The Shadow is a drone launched from a catapult on the back of a truck and recovered by an arrestor cable, because it has no undercarriage worth landing on. It is tactical rather than strategic: a brigade's own eyes, operated by soldiers rather than by a distant crew.

The airframe holds 130,717 polygons and 135,721 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $119 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.
